description:
## Background

The canonical TypeScript quality check, `mise run ts:check`, currently fails for two reasons: formatting differences in 18 tracked files and lint violations in existing source, test, and E2E code. The failures prevent `mise run verify` from passing even though the TypeScript and Rust test suites pass.

The formatting findings currently include:

- `.pi/agents/worker.md`
- `.pi/chains/implement-bead.chain.md`
- `.pi/prompts/implement-bead.md`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `CONTEXT.md`
- `docs/adr/0007-refresh-issue-list-by-polling-beadwork-ref.md`
- `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`
- `docs/agents/webdriver-e2e.md`
- `docs/research/cross-environment-gate-acceptance.md`
- `docs/research/workspace-management-verification-and-migration.md`
- `src/App.tsx`
- `src/components/Sidebar.tsx`
- `src/components/Titlebar.tsx`
- `src/components/WorkspaceSelector.tsx`
- `src/components/ui/Alert.tsx`
- `src/issues/IssueExplorer.tsx`
- `src/issues/RefreshFailureBanner.tsx`
- `src/settings/SettingsPage.tsx`

## What to build

Bring the repository's current TypeScript, React, E2E, and documentation files into compliance with the configured Ultracite formatter and linter. This is a mechanical quality cleanup: preserve runtime behavior, test assertions, accessibility semantics, and public contracts.

## Technical Approach

- Use `mise run fix` where appropriate to apply the repository's canonical formatting fixes, then review the diff for unintended changes.
- Resolve the reported lint findings rather than adding rule suppressions. The current findings include React ref access during render, component naming/definition rules, JSX curly-brace simplification, `no-void`, direct re-export preferences, handler naming, hardcoded Tailwind colors, React rule suppression, numeric coercion, and redundant returns.
- Pay particular attention to the current findings in:
  - `src/issues/use-issue-navigation-coordinator.ts`
  - `src/issues/use-workspace-coordinator.ts`
  - `src/issues/IssueExplorer.tsx`
  - `src/App.tsx`
  - `src/components/MarkdownContent.tsx`
  - `src/components/MarkdownContent.test.tsx`
  - `src/components/mermaid/MermaidDiagram.tsx`
  - `src/components/Titlebar.tsx`
  - `src/settings/SettingsPage.tsx`
  - `src/lib/use-external-lifecycle.ts`
  - `src/rpc/bindings.ts`
  - `e2e/settings/settings-helpers.ts`
- For React ref diagnostics, restructure code so render remains pure and refs are read only in effects or event handlers; do not add suppressions to preserve the current shape.
- For hardcoded colors, use an existing design token or the appropriate theme token instead of weakening the Tailwind rule.
- Re-run the focused quality task until it passes, then run the full verification gate.

## Considerations

- Some findings are in documentation and agent files, not only application code; include all files reported by the formatter.
- Avoid drive-by refactors, behavior changes, or test rewrites unrelated to the reported findings.
- Preserve generated-file conventions for `src/rpc/bindings.ts`; if the file is generated, update the source/generation path rather than hand-editing generated output without documenting why.
- Keep the current 384 passing Vitest tests and 178 passing Rust tests passing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mise run ts:check` passes with no formatting or lint errors.
- [ ] All currently reported formatting findings are resolved.
- [ ] No new broad lint suppressions, disabled rules, or hardcoded color exceptions are introduced.
- [ ] Existing application behavior, test assertions, accessibility semantics, and generated RPC contracts are preserved.
- [ ] `mise run ts:test` continues to pass.

## Test Plan

- Run `mise run ts:check`.
- Run `mise run ts:test`.
- Run `mise run ts:typecheck`.
- After the TypeScript configuration child task is complete, run `mise run verify`.

## Triage
